stemBlocks.value: Think first: The minus sign in the middle means the second pair needs a negative factor taken out.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p092-q03 from workbook page 92.

solutionSteps.instruction: Take the common factor out of each pair.

contentBlocks.value: 4x from the first pair; −5 from the second so that the bracket matches

strategyBlocks.value: Group in pairs, take out 4x from the first pair and −5 from the second so that the brackets match, then take out the common bracket.

whyThisWorks.value: Pulling out a negative factor from the second pair is what makes the two brackets identical; with +5 the signs inside would be reversed and nothing would cancel. Once the brackets match, the common bracket factors out like any other common factor.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking out +5 instead of −5, leaving (2x + 3y) and (−2x − 3y).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking out +5 instead of −5, leaving (2x + 3y) and (−2x − 3y).

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to change the signs inside the bracket after removing a negative factor.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to change the signs inside the bracket after removing a negative factor.

commonErrors.misconception: Leaving the answer as a sum of two products instead of a single product.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Leaving the answer as a sum of two products instead of a single product.

examTip.value: When the third term is negative, plan from the start to take a negative factor out of the second pair.
